{"author":{"id":"MDQ6VXNlcjEwNDk5Mjk3","is_bot":false,"login":"xzyaoi","name":"Xiaozhe Yao"},"body":"## Summary

`vk_hip_dsa_sparse_fwd` (PR #52) documents a set of input preconditions in `src/c/vkernels/kernels/dsa.hpp:69-75` but enforces **none** of them in the host launch path (`dsa.cpp` / `dsa.hip`). An unmet precondition does not raise — it launches a kernel that silently never returns, leaving the scheduler stuck in uninterruptible GPU-driver sleep (`D` state) with no `cudaGetLastError`, no Python traceback, and no `SIGQUIT`. This is exactly the signature that made the GLM-5.3-Flash decode bring-up on MI300A (gfx942) painful to diagnose, and it is a trap for any future caller of the C ABI (PR #44).

Flagged as a separable gap in #56; filing standalone per maintainer request.

## Documented preconditions (dsa.hpp:69-75)

```
69: //   d_v = dim - tail_dim   (must be > 0; tail_dim may be 0)
70: //   topk % (block_I * inner_iter) must be 0 (the kernel's group tiling; the
71: //       oracle result is grouping-independent so this is validated, not used)
72: //   kv_group must be 1 (a single head_kv group is shared by all H heads)
...
32: //   indices : [1, S_q, kv_group, topk] int32  (padded to a multiple of 64;
...
74: // `lse` may be null when `return_lse` is false; otherwise it must be large
75: // enough for `S_q * H` fp32 values. `out` must not alias any input.
```

## What's enforced today

`dsa.cpp` host entry has only a no-op early return (`if (S_q == 0 || H == 0 || topk == 0) return;` at `:44`) and in-kernel masking of out-of-range `idx` (`:63`) and all-masked rows (`:75`). `dsa.hip` has only tile selection by `bq` (`:196-202`) before the launch at `:178`. There is **no** `TORCH_CHECK`/`assert`/`c10::` check for any of the documented preconditions on either the CPU oracle (`dsa.cpp`) or the HIP kernel (`dsa.hip`) launch path. (PR #54 added `checked_mul` coverage elsewhere; the DSA launch path is the remaining gap.)

## Impact (observed)

- **Silent hang, not a crash.** A caller passing e.g. `kv_group != 1`, `topk` not divisible by `block_I*inner_iter`, `d_v <= 0`, or `out` aliasing an input gets a launched kernel that does not return. Reproducible signature from GLM-5.3 decode (job 613311, opentela-ai/cookbook): all four `scheduler_TP{0..3}_EP{0..3}` enter `Dl` state; fwd-probe tally ENTER 584 / EXIT 0; sbatch health gate gives up at 900s.
- **Hard to localize.** The `D` state blocks `py-spy dump` and even `/proc/<pid>/syscall` reads past their timeouts, so the only diagnostics are non-blocking `/proc` (state + wchan) and the log. A `TORCH_CHECK` at launch would have named the bad input in milliseconds.
- **ABI trap.** PR #44's C ABI exposes `vk_hip_dsa_sparse_fwd` to external callers (the opentela-ai/cookbook GLM-5.3 serving path binds it directly via `vkernels_dsa.py`). Those callers have no way to discover the preconditions except by reading the header comment — and no way to get a error if they violate one.

## Proposed fix

Add `TORCH_CHECK` (or equivalent `SGL_CHECK`/`c10::`/`assert`) at the top of the host launch path in `dsa.cpp` **and** `dsa.hip`, mirroring the documented preconditions:

```c
TORCH_CHECK(d_v > 0, "dim must exceed tail_dim (d_v = dim - tail_dim > 0), got d_v=", d_v);
TORCH_CHECK(kv_group == 1, "kv_group must be 1 (single head_kv shared by all H), got ", kv_group);
TORCH_CHECK(topk % (block_I * inner_iter) == 0,
            "topk must be a multiple of block_I*inner_iter (", block_I, "*", inner_iter,
            "): got topk=", topk);
TORCH_CHECK(indices_dim % 64 == 0, "indices last dim must be padded to a multiple of 64, got ", indices_dim);
TORCH_CHECK(out != q && out != kv && out != indices, "out must not alias any input");
if (return_lse) TORCH_CHECK(lse != nullptr, "return_lse=true requires non-null lse (S_q*H fp32)");
```

(Exact symbol names to match the file's existing convention; `dsa.hpp:70-71` notes `topk % (block_I*inner_iter)` is validated-but-not-used, so the check should be cheap and unconditional.)

This converts the silent hang into a named, debuggable error and documents the contract at the one place a C-ABI caller can reach it. It will also **speed up** root-causing #56's decode hang, since the first thing to rule out is "the transform step fed `sparse_fwd` a precondition-violating input."

## Repro

Any caller passing a precondition-violating input to `vk_hip_dsa_sparse_fwd` on gfx942. The GLM-5.3-Flash decode path in `opentela-ai/cookbook` (`deployments/llm/beverin/glm-53-flash/`, job 613311) exhibits the silent-hang signature; the attached checks would identify whether the decode-path inputs violate the `sparse_fwd` contract.","number":57,"state":"OPEN","title":"bug(amd): DSA sparse-fwd preconditions are documented but unenforced (silent gfx942 hang)","url":"https://github.com/opentela-ai/vkernels/issues/57"}

Author: Xiaozhe Yao <askxzyao@gmail.com>

    fix(main): unblock CI after 181d9f9 (per-key-dim gate OOB + checked_mul coverage) (#54)
    
    * test(capi): size K3 naive gate per-key-dim [B,H,S,D] and re-scope oracle
    
    CapiKda.NaiveDeltaRuleFwd and CapiKda.DeltaRuleFwdMatchesNaive (added in

    passed it to vk_kda_naive_delta_rule_fwd, whose contract is the K3

    masked-by-!isnan assertions into a ~1e+22 blow-up -- the C++ CTest that
    has blocked every main PR (and PR #47) since.
    
      * NaiveDeltaRuleFwd: allocate g as [B,H,S,D] (0.5 per key-dim) and
        assert every output element (hand-derived o0=o1=[1,1]).

        g [B,H,S,D]) and the chunked forward (standard, pre-gate,
        g [B,H,S]) are DIFFERENT recurrences since #45 and only agree at
        g==1, where the gate is the identity in both. Cross-check at g==1
        with random q/k/v/beta and a 1e-3 sentinel (measured ~1.8e-7 at
        g==1 -- loose enough to survive toolchain FP drift, tight enough
        to catch the old 1e+22 divergence).

        visible at the ABI.

    against; the device ABI is bf16 (the integrator converts).

    relevant KV tiles (``indices``); this kernel scores each query against
    those keys and produces the combined attention output.

    def test_hand_checked_tail_dim_zero(self):
        # GLM-5.3-Flash (tail_dim == 0). q=[1,1], 2 keys, sm_scale=1:
        # scores {1,1} -> base-2 weights {1,1}/2 -> out {0.5,0.5}, lse=2.
        q = np.array([1, 1], dtype=_F32).reshape(1, 1, 1, 2)
        kv = np.array([1, 0, 0, 1], dtype=_F32).reshape(1, 2, 1, 2)

        out, lse = dsa_sparse_fwd(q, kv, idx, dim=2, tail_dim=0,
                                  sm_scale=1.0, return_lse=True)
        self.assertEqual(out.shape, (1, 1, 1, 2))
        self.assertEqual(out.dtype, _F32)
        np.testing.assert_allclose(out[0, 0, 0], [0.5, 0.5], atol=1e-6)

def dsa_sparse_fwd(q, kv, indices, *, dim, tail_dim, topk=None,
                   kv_group=1, block_I=64, inner_iter=1, sm_scale=None,
                   return_lse=False, out=None, lse=None):
    """DeepseekSparseAttn sparse-MLA forward (GLM-5.3-Flash / DeepSeek-V3),
    fp32 two-pass BASE-2 stable softmax over the ``topk`` indexer-selected
    keys. This is the CPU reference the gfx942 HIP kernel is checked
    against; the device ABI is bf16 (the integrator converts).

    The indexer has already selected, per query token, the ``topk`` most
    relevant KV tiles (``indices``); this kernel scores each query against
    those keys and produces the combined attention output.

    * ``q``       : ``(1, S_q,  H,  dim + tail_dim)`` float32 —
                   ``[q_main (dim) | q_tail (tail_dim)]`` (tail may be 0).
    * ``kv``      : ``(1, S_kv, kv_group, dim + tail_dim)`` float32 (kv_group==1)
                   ``kv[j] = [v (d_v) | k_nope_extra (tail_dim) | k_rope (tail_dim)]``
                   so ``v = kv[j][0:d_v]``, ``k_main = kv[j][0:dim]``,
                   ``k_tail = kv[j][dim:dim+tail_dim]``, with ``d_v = dim - tail_dim``.
    * ``indices`` : ``(1, S_q, kv_group, topk)`` int32 — selected key ids;
                   entries ``< 0`` or ``>= S_kv`` are masked kpool tails.
    * ``out``     : ``(1, S_q, H, d_v)`` float32 (combined).
    * ``lse``     : ``(1, S_q, H)`` float32 (base-2 log-sum-exp; optional).

    ``dim`` and ``tail_dim`` are passed explicitly (they are not separately
    recoverable from ``W = dim + tail_dim``). ``d_v = dim - tail_dim`` must be
    positive. ``sm_scale`` defaults to ``(1/sqrt(dim + tail_dim)) * log2(e)``
    (the base-2 fold); ``tail_dim == 0`` skips the rope-tail dot entirely —
    the exact case the tilelang code path cannot compile.

    Args:
        q: float32 ``(1, S_q, H, dim + tail_dim)`` queries.
        kv: float32 ``(1, S_kv, kv_group, dim + tail_dim)`` keys/values.
        indices: int32 ``(1, S_q, kv_group, topk)`` selected key ids.
        dim: the main key/query width (``qk_nope_head_dim + qk_rope_head_dim``
            in the absorbed form).
        tail_dim: the decoupled RoPE tail width (may be 0).
        topk: number of selected keys per query. Inferred from ``indices``
            when omitted.
        kv_group: number of key/value heads (must be 1).
        block_I, inner_iter: kernel group-tiling configuration (the indexer
            pads ``topk`` to a multiple of ``block_I`` in the sglang layout).
        sm_scale: softmax pre-scale (folds ``log2(e)``); defaults to
            ``(1/sqrt(dim + tail_dim)) * log2(e)``.
        return_lse: when True, also compute the base-2 log-sum-exp.
        out: optional writable float32 ``(1, S_q, H, d_v)`` buffer.
        lse: optional writable float32 ``(1, S_q, H)`` buffer (required
            only when ``return_lse=True``).

    Returns:
        ``out`` when ``return_lse=False``, otherwise ``(out, lse)``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: on inconsistent shapes, ``d_v <= 0``, or ``kv_group != 1``.
    """
    q_arr = _as_input(q, "q")
    kv_arr = _as_input(kv, "kv")
    idx_arr = np.ascontiguousarray(indices, dtype=np.int32)
    if idx_arr.dtype != np.int32:
        raise TypeError("indices must be an integer array")
    if q_arr.ndim != 4:
        raise ValueError("q must be 4-D [1, S_q, H, dim + tail_dim]")
    if kv_arr.ndim != 4:

    (``<0/>=S_kv`` masked), ``W = dim + tail_dim``, ``d_v = dim - tail_dim``.

    d_v = dim - tail_dim

    kv = np.ascontiguousarray(kv, dtype=np.float32).reshape(S_kv, W)
    idx = np.ascontiguousarray(indices, dtype=np.int32).reshape(S_q, topk)
    out = np.ascontiguousarray(out, dtype=np.float32).reshape(S_q, H, d_v)
    lse = (
        np.ascontiguousarray(lse, dtype=np.float32).reshape(S_q, H)
        if return_lse
        else None
    )
    for i in range(S_q):
        idx_i = idx[i]  # (topk,)
        valid = (idx_i >= 0) & (idx_i < S_kv)  # (topk,)
        sel = np.where(valid, idx_i, 0)  # safe gather index
        kv_sel = kv[sel]  # (topk, W)
        v_sel = kv_sel[:, :d_v]  # (topk, d_v)
        k_main = kv_sel[:, :dim]  # (topk, dim)
        q_i = q[i]  # (H, W)
        q_main = q_i[:, :dim]  # (H, dim)
        s = q_main @ k_main.T  # (H, topk)

#4 [tool_result] {"author":{"id":"MDQ6VXNlcjEwNDk5Mjk3","is_bot":false,"login":"xzyaoi","name":"Xiaozhe Yao"},"body":"## Summary

`vk_hip_dsa_sparse_fwd` (PR #52) documents a set of input preconditions in `src/c/vkernels/kernels/dsa.hpp:69-75` but enforces **none** of them in the host launch path (`dsa.cpp` / `dsa.hip`). An unmet precondition does not raise — it launches a kernel that silently never returns, leaving the scheduler stuck in uninterruptible GPU-driver sleep (`D` state) with no `cudaGetLastError`, no Python traceback, and no `SIGQUIT`. This is exactly the signature that made the GLM-5.3-Flash decode bring-up on MI300A (gfx942) painful to diagnose, and it is a trap for any future caller of the C ABI (PR #44).

Flagged as a separable gap in #56; filing standalone per maintainer request.

## Documented preconditions (dsa.hpp:69-75)

```
69: //   d_v = dim - tail_dim   (must be > 0; tail_dim may be 0)
70: //   topk % (block_I * inner_iter) must be 0 (the kernel's group tiling; the
71: //       oracle result is grouping-independent so this is validated, not used)
72: //   kv_group must be 1 (a single head_kv group is shared by all H heads)
...
32: //   indices : [1, S_q, kv_group, topk] int32  (padded to a multiple of 64;
...
74: // `lse` may be null when `return_lse` is false; otherwise it must be large
75: // enough for `S_q * H` fp32 values. `out` must not alias any input.
```

## What's enforced today

`dsa.cpp` host entry has only a no-op early return (`if (S_q == 0 || H == 0 || topk == 0) return;` at `:44`) and in-kernel masking of out-of-range `idx` (`:63`) and all-masked rows (`:75`). `dsa.hip` has only tile selection by `bq` (`:196-202`) before the launch at `:178`. There is **no** `TORCH_CHECK`/`assert`/`c10::` check for any of the documented preconditions on either the CPU oracle (`dsa.cpp`) or the HIP kernel (`dsa.hip`) launch path. (PR #54 added `checked_mul` coverage elsewhere; the DSA launch path is the remaining gap.)

## Impact (observed)

- **Silent hang, not a crash.** A caller passing e.g. `kv_group != 1`, `topk` not divisible by `block_I*inner_iter`, `d_v <= 0`, or `out` aliasing an input gets a launched kernel that does not return. Reproducible signature from GLM-5.3 decode (job 613311, opentela-ai/cookbook): all four `scheduler_TP{0..3}_EP{0..3}` enter `Dl` state; fwd-probe tally ENTER 584 / EXIT 0; sbatch health gate gives up at 900s.
- **Hard to localize.** The `D` state blocks `py-spy dump` and even `/proc/<pid>/syscall` reads past their timeouts, so the only diagnostics are non-blocking `/proc` (state + wchan) and the log. A `TORCH_CHECK` at launch would have named the bad input in milliseconds.
- **ABI trap.** PR #44's C ABI exposes `vk_hip_dsa_sparse_fwd` to external callers (the opentela-ai/cookbook GLM-5.3 serving path binds it directly via `vkernels_dsa.py`). Those callers have no way to discover the preconditions except by reading the header comment — and no way to get a error if they violate one.

## Proposed fix

Add `TORCH_CHECK` (or equivalent `SGL_CHECK`/`c10::`/`assert`) at the top of the host launch path in `dsa.cpp` **and** `dsa.hip`, mirroring the documented preconditions:

```c
TORCH_CHECK(d_v > 0, "dim must exceed tail_dim (d_v = dim - tail_dim > 0), got d_v=", d_v);
TORCH_CHECK(kv_group == 1, "kv_group must be 1 (single head_kv shared by all H), got ", kv_group);
TORCH_CHECK(topk % (block_I * inner_iter) == 0,
            "topk must be a multiple of block_I*inner_iter (", block_I, "*", inner_iter,
            "): got topk=", topk);
TORCH_CHECK(indices_dim % 64 == 0, "indices last dim must be padded to a multiple of 64, got ", indices_dim);
TORCH_CHECK(out != q && out != kv && out != indices, "out must not alias any input");
if (return_lse) TORCH_CHECK(lse != nullptr, "return_lse=true requires non-null lse (S_q*H fp32)");
```

(Exact symbol names to match the file's existing convention; `dsa.hpp:70-71` notes `topk % (block_I*inner_iter)` is validated-but-not-used, so the check should be cheap and unconditional.)

This converts the silent hang into a named, debuggable error and documents the contract at the one place a C-ABI caller can reach it. It will also **speed up** root-causing #56's decode hang, since the first thing to rule out is "the transform step fed `sparse_fwd` a precondition-violating input."

## Repro

Any caller passing a precondition-violating input to `vk_hip_dsa_sparse_fwd` on gfx942. # Issue #57: DSA sparse-fwd preconditions enforced (silent gfx942 hang)

## Problem
`dsa_sparse_fwd_cpu` (dsa.cpp) and the HIP `dsa_sparse_fwd`/`dsa_sparse_fwd_with_tile`
(dsa.hip) DOCUMENTED preconditions in `dsa.hpp:69-75` but enforced NONE. An
unmet precondition launched a kernel that silently never returned (`D`-state hang
on gfx942, no traceback, hard to localize).

## Enforced preconditions (on BOTH dsa.cpp and dsa.hip, plus C ABI + Python)
- `d_v = dim - tail_dim > 0`
- `topk % (block_I * inner_iter) == 0`
- `kv_group == 1`
- `out` must not alias `q`, `kv`, `indices`, `lse` (two-pass softmax writes a row
  into `out` then reads it back; shared buffer corrupts the run)
- `lse != nullptr` when `return_lse`

Used `VK_EXPECTS` (repo's `TORCH_CHECK` equivalent; `error.hpp` throws
`std::invalid_argument` on host, no-op on device).

## Key decisions
- **`dsa_config_for` block_I fix**: block_I = largest power-of-two divisor of
  `topk` that is `<= 64` (was hardcoded 64). Ensures `topk % (block_I*inner_iter)
  == 0` for EVERY `topk` (including decode shapes `topk < 64`). The existing
  `topk=2` tests now pass `block_I=2` instead of the old hardcoded `64` (which
  the new divisibility check rejects: `2 % (64*1) != 0`).
- **`indices_dim % 64 == 0` from the issue's proposed fix was NOT added**: the
  CPU oracle / HIP kernel / C API all take `topk` directly (no separate padded
  `indices_dim`/stride). The kernel iterates `for (k < topk)` — any `topk ≥ 1`
  works. "Padded to a multiple of 64" (dsa.hpp:32) is a sglang PHYSICAL-tensor
  caller convention, not a kernel-enforced precondition. Adding `topk % 64 == 0`
  would break the documented happy path (`topk=2` tests) and contradict the
  issue's own guidance ("never blocks the happy path because dsa_config_for is
  always called first").
- **`vk_hip_dsa_sparse_fwd` ABI: void → int**: the HIP C ABI wrapper was `void`
  with no try/catch — a thrown `VK_EXPECTS` would escape the C ABI (UB →
  `std::terminate`). Changed to return `VK_OK`/`VK_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT` with
  explicit host-side validation + try/catch (mirrors `vk_hip_moe_align_block_size`
  and the CPU `vk_dsa_sparse_fwd`). No Python ctypes caller existed (safe change).
- **Exposed `vk_set_last_error(int, const char*)`** in capi.hpp/capi.cpp: the HIP
  C ABI (hip_capi.cpp) does NOT link the `VK_CAPI_TRY` macro or `g_last_error`
  (internal to capi.cpp). The setter lets `vk_hip_*` wrappers record errors the
  same way the CPU wrappers do, so `vk_last_error_code()` works for external callers.

## Verification
- C++ `test_dsa`: 22/22 (added DivisibilityCheckThrows, AliasThrows)
- C API `test_capi` CapiDsa*: 100/100 (added DivisibilityCheckThrows, AliasThrows)
- Python `test_kernels` Dsa*: 28/28 (added test_divisibility_check, test_alias_check)
- Full Python suite: 15 failed / 243 passed vs. TRUE original baseline 15 failed /
  241 passed — SAME 15 pre-existing failures (KDA + discovery, unrelated to DSA),
  +2 new passing DSA tests. Zero new failures.

- `src/c/vkernels/kernels/dsa.cpp` (preconditions + dsa_config_for block_I fix)
- `src/c/vkernels/kernels/dsa.hip` (preconditions on dsa_sparse_fwd + _with_tile)
- `src/c/vkernels/kernels/dsa.hpp` (docstring)
- `src/c/vkernels/capi/capi.{cpp,hpp}` (vk_set_last_error)
- `src/c/vkernels/capi/hip_capi.{cpp,hpp}` (vk_hip_dsa_sparse_fwd: void→int)
- `src/python/vkernels/{kernels,_fallback}.py` (preconditions + dsa_config fix,
  block_I/inner_iter default to None→dsa_config())
- `tests/{kernels/attn/test_dsa,capi/test_capi,python/test_kernels}.cpp/.py`

# Issue #57: DSA sparse-fwd preconditions enforced (silent gfx942 hang)

## Problem
`dsa_sparse_fwd_cpu` (dsa.cpp) and the HIP `dsa_sparse_fwd`/`dsa_sparse_fwd_with_tile`
(dsa.hip) DOCUMENTED preconditions in `dsa.hpp:69-75` but enforced NONE. An
unmet precondition launched a kernel that silently never returned (`D`-state hang
on gfx942, no traceback, hard to localize).

## Enforced preconditions (on BOTH dsa.cpp and dsa.hip, plus C ABI + Python)
- `d_v = dim - tail_dim > 0`
- `topk % (block_I * inner_iter) == 0`
- `kv_group == 1`
- `out` must not alias `q`, `kv`, `indices`, `lse` (two-pass softmax writes a row
  into `out` then reads it back; shared buffer corrupts the run)
- `lse != nullptr` when `return_lse`

Used `VK_EXPECTS` (repo's `TORCH_CHECK` equivalent; `error.hpp` throws
`std::invalid_argument` on host, no-op on device).

## Key decisions
- **`dsa_config_for` block_I fix**: block_I = largest power-of-two divisor of
  `topk` that is `<= 64` (was hardcoded 64). Ensures `topk % (block_I*inner_iter)
  == 0` for EVERY `topk` (including decode shapes `topk < 64`). The existing
  `topk=2` tests now pass `block_I=2` instead of the old hardcoded `64` (which
  the new divisibility check rejects: `2 % (64*1) != 0`).
- **`indices_dim % 64 == 0` from the issue's proposed fix was NOT added**: the
  CPU oracle / HIP kernel / C API all take `topk` directly (no separate padded
  `indices_dim`/stride). The kernel iterates `for (k < topk)` — any `topk ≥ 1`
  works. "Padded to a multiple of 64" (dsa.hpp:32) is a sglang PHYSICAL-tensor
  caller convention, not a kernel-enforced precondition. Adding `topk % 64 == 0`
  would break the documented happy path (`topk=2` tests) and contradict the
  issue's own guidance ("never blocks the happy path because dsa_config_for is
  always called first").
- **`vk_hip_dsa_sparse_fwd` ABI: void → int**: the HIP C ABI wrapper was `void`
  with no try/catch — a thrown `VK_EXPECTS` would escape the C ABI (UB →
  `std::terminate`). Changed to return `VK_OK`/`VK_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT` with
  explicit host-side validation + try/catch (mirrors `vk_hip_moe_align_block_size`
  and the CPU `vk_dsa_sparse_fwd`). No Python ctypes caller existed (safe change).
- **Exposed `vk_set_last_error(int, const char*)`** in capi.hpp/capi.cpp: the HIP
  C ABI (hip_capi.cpp) does NOT link the `VK_CAPI_TRY` macro or `g_last_error`
  (internal to capi.cpp). The setter lets `vk_hip_*` wrappers record errors the
  same way the CPU wrappers do, so `vk_last_error_code()` works for external callers.

## Verification
- C++ `test_dsa`: 22/22 (added DivisibilityCheckThrows, AliasThrows)
- C API `test_capi` CapiDsa*: 100/100 (added DivisibilityCheckThrows, AliasThrows)
- Python `test_kernels` Dsa*: 28/28 (added test_divisibility_check, test_alias_check)
- Full Python suite: 15 failed / 243 passed vs. TRUE original baseline 15 failed /
  241 passed — SAME 15 pre-existing failures (KDA + discovery, unrelated to DSA),
  +2 new passing DSA tests. Zero new failures.

## Files
- `src/c/vkernels/kernels/dsa.cpp` (preconditions + dsa_config_for block_I fix)
- `src/c/vkernels/kernels/dsa.hip` (preconditions on dsa_sparse_fwd + _with_tile)
- `src/c/vkernels/kernels/dsa.hpp` (docstring)
- `src/c/vkernels/capi/capi.{cpp,hpp}` (vk_set_last_error)
- `src/c/vkernels/capi/hip_capi.{cpp,hpp}` (vk_hip_dsa_sparse_fwd: void→int)
- `src/python/vkernels/{kernels,_fallback}.py` (preconditions + dsa_config fix,
  block_I/inner_iter default to None→dsa_config())
- `tests/{kernels/attn/test_dsa,capi/test_capi,python/test_kernels}.cpp/.py`

  works. "Padded to a multiple of 64" (dsa.hpp:32) is a sglang PHYSICAL-tensor
  caller convention, not a kernel-enforced precondition. Adding `topk % 64 == 0`
  would break the documented happy path (`topk=2` tests) and contradict the
  issue's own guidance ("never blocks the happy path because dsa_config_for is
  always called first").
- **`vk_hip_dsa_sparse_fwd` ABI: void → int**: the HIP C ABI wrapper was `void`
  with no try/catch — a thrown `VK_EXPECTS` would escape the C ABI (UB →
  `std::terminate`). Changed to return `VK_OK`/`VK_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT` with
  explicit host-side validation + try/catch (mirrors `vk_hip_moe_align_block_size`
  and the CPU `vk_dsa_sparse_fwd`). No Python ctypes caller existed (safe change).
- **Exposed `vk_set_last_error(int, const char*)`** in capi.hpp/capi.cpp: the HIP
  C ABI (hip_capi.cpp) does NOT link the `VK_CAPI_TRY` macro or `g_last_error`
  (internal to capi.cpp). The setter lets `vk_hip_*` wrappers record errors the
  same way the CPU wrappers do, so `vk_last_error_code()` works for external callers.

  # transport -- the kernel-level surface for the issue, just as
  # bench_pipeline_boundary.cu is for #10. The C ABI symbols live in the

state:	OPEN

## Summary

`vk_hip_dsa_sparse_fwd` (PR #52) documents a set of input preconditions in `src/c/vkernels/kernels/dsa.hpp:69-75` but enforces **none** of them in the host launch path (`dsa.cpp` / `dsa.hip`). An unmet precondition does not raise — it launches a kernel that silently never returns, leaving the scheduler stuck in uninterruptible GPU-driver sleep (`D` state) with no `cudaGetLastError`, no Python traceback, and no `SIGQUIT`. This is exactly the signature that made the GLM-5.3-Flash decode bring-up on MI300A (gfx942) painful to diagnose, and it is a trap for any future caller of the C ABI (PR #44).

Flagged as a separable gap in #56; filing standalone per maintainer request.

## Documented preconditions (dsa.hpp:69-75)

```
69: //   d_v = dim - tail_dim   (must be > 0; tail_dim may be 0)
70: //   topk % (block_I * inner_iter) must be 0 (the kernel's group tiling; the
71: //       oracle result is grouping-independent so this is validated, not used)
72: //   kv_group must be 1 (a single head_kv group is shared by all H heads)
...
32: //   indices : [1, S_q, kv_group, topk] int32  (padded to a multiple of 64;
...
74: // `lse` may be null when `return_lse` is false; otherwise it must be large
75: // enough for `S_q * H` fp32 values. `out` must not alias any input.
```

## What's enforced today

`dsa.cpp` host entry has only a no-op early return (`if (S_q == 0 || H == 0 || topk == 0) return;` at `:44`) and in-kernel masking of out-of-range `idx` (`:63`) and all-masked rows (`:75`). `dsa.hip` has only tile selection by `bq` (`:196-202`) before the launch at `:178`. There is **no** `TORCH_CHECK`/`assert`/`c10::` check for any of the documented preconditions on either the CPU oracle (`dsa.cpp`) or the HIP kernel (`dsa.hip`) launch path. (PR #54 added `checked_mul` coverage elsewhere; the DSA launch path is the remaining gap.)

## Impact (observed)

- **Silent hang, not a crash.** A caller passing e.g. `kv_group != 1`, `topk` not divisible by `block_I*inner_iter`, `d_v <= 0`, or `out` aliasing an input gets a launched kernel that does not return. Reproducible signature from GLM-5.3 decode (job 613311, opentela-ai/cookbook): all four `scheduler_TP{0..3}_EP{0..3}` enter `Dl` state; fwd-probe tally ENTER 584 / EXIT 0; sbatch health gate gives up at 900s.
- **Hard to localize.** The `D` state blocks `py-spy dump` and even `/proc/<pid>/syscall` reads past their timeouts, so the only diagnostics are non-blocking `/proc` (state + wchan) and the log. A `TORCH_CHECK` at launch would have named the bad input in milliseconds.
- **ABI trap.** PR #44's C ABI exposes `vk_hip_dsa_sparse_fwd` to external callers (the opentela-ai/cookbook GLM-5.3 serving path binds it directly via `vkernels_dsa.py`). Those callers have no way to discover the preconditions except by reading the header comment — and no way to get a error if they violate one.

## Proposed fix

Add `TORCH_CHECK` (or equivalent `SGL_CHECK`/`c10::`/`assert`) at the top of the host launch path in `dsa.cpp` **and** `dsa.hip`, mirroring the documented preconditions:

```c
TORCH_CHECK(d_v > 0, "dim must exceed tail_dim (d_v = dim - tail_dim > 0), got d_v=", d_v);
TORCH_CHECK(kv_group == 1, "kv_group must be 1 (single head_kv shared by all H), got ", kv_group);
TORCH_CHECK(topk % (block_I * inner_iter) == 0,
            "topk must be a multiple of block_I*inner_iter (", block_I, "*", inner_iter,
            "): got topk=", topk);
TORCH_CHECK(indices_dim % 64 == 0, "indices last dim must be padded to a multiple of 64, got ", indices_dim);
TORCH_CHECK(out != q && out != kv && out != indices, "out must not alias any input");
if (return_lse) TORCH_CHECK(lse != nullptr, "return_lse=true requires non-null lse (S_q*H fp32)");
```
